items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: going to work for this Mr. Cooper, a very nice gentleman, and he taught me how to drive.

ctx.x: No, not music, a way of life. The way of life. Because, you know, it was rough and you had to come through that. You had to. It was quite an experience, and I felt like I was really developed into manhood when I, at the age of 19... there was no question about it.

And at the age of 14, like I said, going to work for this Mr. Cooper, a very nice gentleman, and he taught me how to drive. I learned how to drive in a Model A truck, a little pickup truck that he had. And that's what we used to go to the coal yard to pick up a ton, half a ton, or whatever we bought, to bring it back to the shed and break it down to bushel baskets.

And that's how I made it. In the winter time we sold coal, summer time we sold ice. So it was all year around for me. Of course, we had a little slow season in the spring and fall because they didn't hardly go too much either way. But I was very happy working with Mr. Cooper, because it gave me a chance to have a job and that meant something. You know, even at age 14, jobs were...there just wasn't anything to have.
